t: Sertoli, Leydig, germ cell or myoid cell?
key: Ask where the cell sits and which pituitary hormone it answers: inside the tubule wall and answering FSH is a Sertoli cell, in the interstitium outside the tubule and answering LH is a Leydig cell, a cell that changes ploidy as it moves toward the lumen is a germ cell, and a contractile cell wrapped around the outside is a myoid cell.
items: Carries the FSH receptor
sertoli
FSH acts only on Sertoli cells inside the tubule, which is why FSH controls sperm support while LH controls testosterone.
Secretes inhibin B, which selectively suppresses FSH
sertoli
Inhibin B travels to the pituitary and lowers FSH alone, so loss of germ cells raises FSH while LH and testosterone stay normal.
Secretes androgen-binding protein
sertoli
It holds testosterone inside the tubule at 50 to 100 times the serum level, the high local concentration that spermatogenesis needs.
Forms tight junctions that create the blood-testis barrier
sertoli
Junctions between neighboring Sertoli cells split the tubule into basal and adluminal compartments and hide meiotic cell antigens from the immune system.
Engulfs the cytoplasm shed by spermatids
sertoli
At the end of spermiogenesis, Sertoli cells phagocytose the residual bodies that spermatids discard as they slim down into sperm.
Secretes anti-Müllerian hormone in the fetus
sertoli
Fetal Sertoli cells make AMH, which causes the Müllerian ducts to regress so that a male fetus has no uterus or tubes.
Carries the LH receptor, and binds hCG as well
leydig
LH and hCG act through the same receptor, so hCG injections stimulate Leydig cells to make testosterone.
Makes testosterone from cholesterol
leydig
Under LH, Leydig cells convert cholesterol to testosterone, and StAR-mediated cholesterol entry into mitochondria is the rate-limiting step.
Contains rod-shaped Reinke crystals
leydig
These crystalloids are the histologic signature of Leydig cells and their tumors, which cause precocious puberty or gynecomastia.
Lies in the interstitium beside capillaries, outside the barrier
leydig
Leydig cells sit between the tubules beside capillaries, so they release testosterone into the blood and nearby tubules without crossing the barrier.
Divides by mitosis on the basement membrane
germ
Spermatogonia are diploid stem cells that renew themselves and send committed daughters inward, so they sit outside the barrier.
Largest and most conspicuous cell on biopsy, with a long meiotic prophase
germ
Primary spermatocytes spend weeks in prophase of meiosis I, so they are the meiotic cell most often caught on a section.
Haploid cell that finishes meiosis II within hours and is rarely seen
germ
The second division is so fast that secondary spermatocytes are seldom caught on a section, and many cells labeled as such are early spermatids.
Remodels without dividing to build an acrosome and a tail
germ
Spermatids undergo spermiogenesis: the Golgi forms the acrosome, a centriole grows the flagellum and the nucleus condenses.
Contractile cell wrapped around the outside of the tubule
myoid
Peritubular myoid cells are smooth-muscle-like cells that surround each tubule, outside the Sertoli cells and basement membrane.
Squeezes sperm along the tubule toward the rete testis
myoid
Sperm are immotile when released, so contraction of the myoid cells and the flow of fluid carry them out of the testis.
